title: Token Cost Atlas: exportable breakdown & pricing patterns
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and prototype a token-level cost analytics interface (Token Cost Atlas) for the Redwood Console that provides: (1) per-route and per-model token cost breakdowns, (2) attribution by API key/team/user and prompt segments, (3) CSV/JSON export patterns, and (4) UI patterns for displaying pricing tiers and custom rates. Deliverables: clickable prototype, interaction spec, export API contract sketch, and design QA checklist.
design_notes: Goals: make cost attribution actionable for engineers and finance; avoid surfacing misleading per-token values (use averaged/attributed estimates where exact billing is complex); enable fast exploration and export for downstream analysis. Primary views: Overview (high-level totals + sparklines), Route Breakdown (stacked token & cost by route), Prompt Attribution (token slices by prompt/template + sample traces), Pricing Inspector (mapping of pricing rules, discounts, committed rate overrides). Interaction patterns: flexible time window, grouping (model/route/team), column chooser, sampling mode toggle for large ranges, background CSV generation for large exports.
comments: 2025-11-05 — Aisha Kumar: Initial wireframes uploaded to Figma. Focused on table-first UX with time-series header and quick filters. Asked ENG for estimated query cost for 90-day ranges.

2025-11-07 — Liam Chen: Engineering review: large-range ad-hoc queries can be expensive. Suggested server-side pre-aggregation for 7/30/90 day buckets and sample-first strategy for >90 days. Raised concern about showing per-token cost for cached responses—need annotation when KV-cache hit reduces marginal cost.

2025-11-09 — Priya Desai (PM): Requested an export schema that includes both 'estimated_cost' and 'billing_units' fields, plus a mapping table for pricing rules applied (tier/discount). Need CSV header naming conventions to align with finance imports.

2025-11-12 — Marcus Lee (Engineering): Prototype CSV generator: supports async export job + signed download link, chunked by route for streaming. Memory guardrails included. Asked design for UX when export is queued/failed.

2025-11-14 — UX Research (Dana Ortiz): Ran 3 sessions with platform engineers. Key insight: users want side-by-side comparison of 'expected billing' vs 'observed spend' for anomaly triage. Request: easily pin a route and see token distribution heatmaps.

2025-11-16 — Security review (K. Nguyen): flagged that user-level attribution may contain PII in prompt snippets. Recommend prompt redaction toggle and default to hashed identifiers in exports unless admin opt-in.
2025-11-18 — Aisha Kumar: Implemented redaction toggle and added export consent modal. Pushing updated prototype and this ticket to In Review for design sign-off.
feedback_summary: Engineering: prefer pre-aggregations and sampling to bound cost; require async export jobs. PM: wants export schema compatible with finance workflows and breakdown of pricing rules. UX Research: users need comparison mode (expected vs observed). Security: require prompt redaction and admin consent for detailed exports.
decisions: Use server-side pre-aggregations for standard windows (7/30/90 days). For ad-hoc >90 days, present sampled estimates with a clear confidence indicator.
Exports use async job model; front-end shows job status, download link when ready, and per-chunk progress. Small exports (<5MB) download synchronously.
Include both 'estimated_cost' (derived) and 'billing_units' (raw tokens/embeddings/requests) in CSV; attach pricing_rule_id and human-readable pricing_rule_name for traceability.
Default to redacted prompt snippets in any UI and export unless admin enables 'Detailed Export' with explicit consent and audit logging.
Pricing Inspector shows active pricing tiers and overrides; hover reveals effective per-token microcost and rationale (commit discount, quantization savings approximation).
Show KV-cache hit annotation per route and adjust marginal cost display when cache hits exceed 20% of tokens.
Support column chooser; default columns: route, model, tokens_input, tokens_output, billing_units, estimated_cost, pricing_rule_name, team, api_key_alias.
Add 'Compare' mode to overlay two date ranges for quick expected vs observed comparisons.
Accessibility: color palettes meet contrast for color-blind users; table supports keyboard navigation and ARIA labels on critical controls.

acceptance_criteria: Clickable Figma prototype covering Overview, Route Breakdown, Prompt Attribution, and Pricing Inspector is available and linked in the ticket.
Export flow mockups include queued/ready/error states, consent modal, and redaction options.
Design spec enumerates default columns and column chooser behavior; includes examples of CSV header names mapping to finance import fields.
All engineering concerns listed in comments have either an implementation note or a design mitigation (sampling, pre-agg, async exports).
Prototype validated by at least 3 research sessions and accessibility checklist passed.
Ownership and next steps assigned and scheduled.
